message: Arabic letter ي, ى or ك: Persian writes ی (U+06CC) and ک (U+06A9) (STYLE 20.4).
Letter of another orthography (ة, ھ, ۀ, ہ, ە): write ه, and write the ezafe after a silent ه as ه + U+0654 (هٔ) (STYLE 20.4).
ASCII comma, semicolon or question mark after Persian text: write ، ؛ ؟ (Microsoft Persian Style Guide 4.1.14).
Persian or Arabic-Indic digit or separator (۰-۹, ٠-٩, ٪, ٫, ٬): numbers keep 0-9 with the English decimal point and grouping (PD-OI-106, campaign D-15).
Verb prefix می or نمی followed by a space: join it with ZWNJ U+200C (می‌شود، نمی‌توان) (Microsoft Persian Style Guide 4.1.17, دستور خط فارسی).
Verb prefix می or نمی written joined to the verb: write ZWNJ U+200C between them (می‌شود، نمی‌کند) (STYLE 20.4).
Plural ها or های joined to a letter that connects: write ZWNJ U+200C before it (فایل‌ها، ویژگی‌های، آن‌ها) (Microsoft Persian Style Guide 4.1.17).
Ezafe after a silent ه written ه‌ی: write هٔ (ه + U+0654), as دستور خط فارسی and Chromium fa do (STYLE 20.4).
Hamza above U+0654 outside the ezafe هٔ: use the letter ئ (U+0626), أ (U+0623) or ؤ (U+0624) (STYLE 20.4).
English or straight quotes in a Persian value: write « » (Microsoft Persian Style Guide 4.1.14); code such as /key="value" keeps its straight quotes.
Space inside « »: write the quoted text against both marks («{name}») (STYLE 20.3).
Space before ، ؛ ؟ : ! or a full stop: attach the mark to the word before it and put one space after it (Microsoft Persian Style Guide 4.1.14).
Three periods or a doubled ellipsis: write one … (U+2026) attached to the word before it (STYLE 1.2).
A hyphen between spaces used as a dash: rewrite with a comma or parentheses (Microsoft Persian Style Guide 4.1.14: em dash to parentheses).

Range written with a dash between two placeholders or an en dash between two numbers: a right-to-left line shows it as end–start; write {start} تا {end} or از … تا … (Microsoft Persian Style Guide 4.1.14; STYLE 20.3).
Arrow → between items of a Persian sentence points against the reading order: write ← (U+2190) for "then" or "becomes"; → stays only in the figure direction راست → (STYLE 20.3).

Persian letter, ZWNJ or plural ها touching a {placeholder} ({file}‌ها, {name}را, فایل{file}): a placeholder takes no suffix; put the class noun before it and write را as its own word (فایل {file} را) (STYLE 20.5).
Latin letter or digit touching a Persian letter (CDS‌ها, 5فایل): put a space between them and no Persian suffix on a Latin word (ویژگی‌های CDS، 5 فایل) (STYLE 20.4).

Persian value starting with a Latin word: an element that takes its direction from its text would read left to right; put the Persian class noun first (برنامهٔ LOSAT، فایل TSV، ترک GC skew) (STYLE 20.3).
Diacritic (haraka, tashdid, sukun, superscript alef): Persian UI text writes none, except the tanwin on alef in adverbs such as لطفاً and دقیقاً (STYLE 20.4).
Tatweel (kashida) ـ: never stretch Persian letters; write the plain word (STYLE 20.4).

Not the glossary word: legend is راهنما (افسانه means a myth), track ترک (not آهنگ), session نشست (not جلسه), file فایل (not پرونده), download بارگیری and upload بارگذاری (not دانلود, آپلود), annotation حاشیه‌نویسی (not شناسه‌گذاری), feature ویژگی (not خصیصه), strain سویه (not کرنش) (STYLE 20.1).
Spelling or word other than the glossary form: write قلم (font), جستجو, در حال, در دسترس, سابقه (history), پیش‌فرض, پیش‌نمایش, بزرگ‌نمایی (zoom), آمینواسید, نرم‌افزار (STYLE 20.1, 20.4).

Leading, trailing or doubled space, an invisible character (NBSP, ZWSP, ZWJ, WJ, BOM), a ZWNJ that does not stand between two Persian letters, or a ZWNJ after a letter that does not join (ا د ذ ر ز ژ و): use single spaces, and ZWNJ only where it keeps two joining letters apart.
Letters of another script (Cyrillic, Hebrew, Devanagari and other Indic scripts, Thai, CJK, kana, Hangul, full-width forms) in a Persian value: a token leak; rewrite in Persian or Latin.
به صورت written with a space: the compound is به‌صورت with ZWNJ U+200C (STYLE 20.4, دستور خط فارسی).
Comma before یا: Persian writes «الف یا ب» with no comma; the comma ، only closes an incidental clause (glossary row «Comma before oppure»). Check that this comma closes one.
